newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CAN SOLVE CRISIS IN TWO YEARS - BALCEROWICZ.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CAN SOLVE CRISIS IN TWO YEARS - BALCEROWICZ.

text.p: Bulgaria can overcome its grave economic crisis in two years if radical steps are taken to liberalise the economy and restore confidence in the currency, former Polish finance minister Leszek Balcerowicz said on Friday.
Balcerowicz, the architect of a tough shock-therapy applied to Poland's ruined economy in 1990, was on a two-day visit to Sofia to advise Bulgaria on reforms.

"Eliminating inflation is a matter of months. Once (financial) discipline is imposed and sustained and the economy rapidly privatised, progress can be achieved in a year or two, but effects will come later," Balcerowicz told reporters.

Cumulative inflation in Bulgaria for the first two months of this year was 392 percent. Balcerowicz said restoring confidence in the lev along with price liberalisation, rapid privatisation and strengthening of institutions was paramount to creating conditions for growth.

"I think that Bulgaria's economic strategy is a sound one and the right one. It is very important once a government is formed to act rapidly and decisively," he said after meeting President Petar Stoyanov on Friday.
But he also warned the authorities that radical therapy would cause considerable pain for society, as it did in Poland in early 1990s.

"Once you launch radical reforms and sustain them there will also be social costs and it is important to inform the people of the choices...there will be unemployment, but there will also be prospects," he said.

Balcerowicz had to quit as finance minister after taking Poland through the initial brunt of market reforms because he became immensely unpopular among hard-hit Poles. However, he has been widely credited by economists with breaking ground for the impressive economic revival in Poland since 1993. He is now heading the opposition Union for Freedom party.
